newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX coming under pressure as FOMC nears.
newsitem.headline: German DAX coming under pressure as FOMC nears.

text.p: German shares were seen following Wall Street's lead after any move on interest rates from the Federal Reserve meeting later on Tuesday but some dealers said the market was heading down, rate rise or not.

"After the price advances of recent weeks, there is clearly a lack of new positive impetus," Trinkhaus Capital Management said, summing up the mood of some market players in an equities study released on Tuesday.
It added however that with German stocks not significantly overvalued at current levels, the consolidation would cease at 3,450-3,500. The IBIS DAX was trading at 3,516.0 by 1347 GMT.

Trinkhaus said a expected consolidation in the bond market and the current debate on taxes going on in Germany -- with a tax on petrol still seen a possibility -- would both help to put the breaks on near-term equity market growth.
The IBIS DAX earlier fell some 50 points to its current level after Wall Street's fall last week.

Dealers also cited a lowering by U.S. investment bank Morgan Stanley of its recommended weighting for German shares. The bank confirmed it had cut its German stock weighting to 16 percent of portfolio from 17.5 percent, still however above its average weighting.
As for the near-term prospects of the market, dealers said no market consensus had formed on what the Federal Reserve would do with interest rates later.
One Frankfurt-based equity salesman noted that the market was as a result less well-prepared for a rate increase than in March, the last time the U.S. authorities tightened credit.
